messages:
maria (PM): quick sync — we need to lock latency buckets + SLO acceptance for Gen2 launch. want alignment by EOD tomorrow so PRD can go final. proposal below.

maria (PM): ```
SLO proposal (client-observed, hosted):
- short-text (<=128 tokens): p50 <120ms, p95 <400ms, p99 <900ms
- long-text (>128 tokens) / chat: p50 <220ms, p95 <700ms, p99 <1500ms
- embeddings: p50 <80ms, p95 <250ms, p99 <600ms
- error budget: 0.1% errors (5xx / malformed) per month
Graceful-degrade: on p99 tail breach for >10m, route to compatible smaller model or cached response; surface degradation banner to customers.
Acceptance criteria:
- Canary (synthetic + shadowed prod) for 48h with no >30% burn of error budget
- Automated perf regression check in CI (diff vs baseline)
- Rollout gating: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%, 2h observation at each step
```

ashwin (SRE): couple Qs: are these end-to-end client-observed latencies (inc network / edge) or just inference time? :thinking_face:

maria (PM): client-observed. we also need an internal inference-time SLO for kernel/runtime teams (separate PRD).

lili (Eng): are we counting streaming responses differently? long chat numbers assume final token completion; streaming p95 will be dominated by tail for first token. maybe split first-byte latency vs last-token?

maria (PM): good call. update: add first-byte target for chat: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 200ms for first token. i'll put this into PRD.

ashwin (SRE): tradeoff: keeping current batching aggressive increases tail. for hosted customers we can pick smarter routing: burst -> dedicated pool with relaxed p95 (500ms) but charge premium. for default hosted we should be conservative.

lili (Eng): sounds reasonable. for embedding-heavy customers we should suggest dedicated or reserve capacity. also we need a fallback model listing in the PRD (id + expected quality delta).

noah (Product): one customer ask: enterprise legal wants 99.5% for SLA on critical endpoints. that's different from SLO. should we propose tiered SLOs (standard vs enterprise)?

maria (PM): yes — propose tiered SLOs in PRD: standard = as above, enterprise = tighten p95 by ~20% and increase monitoring/alerts; enterprise SLA is contractual and will have capacity commit.

ashwin (SRE): canary run command (infra):
```bash
# start synthetics canary against canary pool
curl -X POST https://infra/api/canary/start -d '{"profile":"gen2-slo-canary","duration":"48h"}'
# check status
curl https://infra/api/canary/status/gen2-slo-canary
```
Use `--shadow=true` to mirror 5% of real traffic.

maria (PM): acceptance checklist I'd like in the PRD (short):
- [ ] PRD SLO table + tiering
- [ ] fallback model mapping + quality delta notes
- [ ] Canary playbook + runbook link
- [ ] CI perf regression gates added
- [ ] Rollout gating policy embedded

lili (Eng): add: perf-run baseline commit id and test corpus must be frozen for the CI gate.

ashwin (SRE): also add TTL & eviction rules for KV cache — that'll affect first-byte.

maria (PM): noted — i'll include both. last item: what counts as a breach event vs transient blip? propose: 10m window exceeding p99 budget triggers incident review; >30m triggers rollback/auto-fallback. open to other thresholds.

ashwin (SRE): +1 to 10m review. recommend automated fallback at 20m (route 25% of traffic to fallback model) and rollback at 40m if still degraded.

noah (Product): :thumbsup: also request explicit customer comms template in PRD for informing enterprise customers during graceful degrade.

maria (PM): will draft comms. action items:
- maria: update PRD with first-byte numbers, tiering, comms template (by EOD tomorrow)
- ashwin: canary scripts + fallback automation playbook (tomorrow morning)
- lili: fallback model list + perf delta matrix (end of day)
- noah: customer SLA language + comms template (EOD)

sre-bot: Canary job gen2-slo-canary scheduled by @ashwin (SRE) — ETA: 48h. :white_check_mark:

maria (PM): thanks all. if nobody objects i'll lock the numbers and push the PRD update later today. :eyes:

lili (Eng): no objections from eng. :+1:

ashwin (SRE): fine from SRE. logging a follow-up RFC for internal inference-time SLOs.

noah (Product): good to go from product.
